To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the enteric nervous system and its neuromediators are important players in the regulation of intestinal inflammation and that the modulation of this neuronal circuitry could represent a novel strategy for the treatment of inflammatory bowel diseases.
the nervous system plays a key role in the regulation of the intestinal immune system and that this interaction is relevant for the pathogenesis of IBD.
The immune system is tightly regulated by the nervous system, in which the vagus nerve plays an important role.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms underlying the regulation of the immune system by the central nervous system.
the study of the neuroimmune axis in the gut.
the study of the immune system in the gastrointestinal tract and its modulation via the nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is an increasing evidence of the role of the gut-brain axis in the pathogenesis of IBD, and that the modulation of this axis may be a novel therapeutic strategy to treat IBD.

a better understanding of the complex interplay between the immune and nervous systems may lead to new and innovative therapeutic approaches to restore immune balance in chronic inflammatory conditions.
a bidirectional communication exists between the brain, the enteric nervous system, and the immune system, which can be modulated by the gut microbiota and that this communication is altered in IBD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immune system is a dynamic, adaptive, and highly regulated system.
the immune system is modulated by the brain and that the brain is also modulated by the immune system.
we are trying to understand the mechanisms that control the balance between immune tolerance and immune activation in the intestine and how this is regulated by the nervous system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a bidirectional cross-talk between the immune system and the nervous system, which can be exploited as a novel therapeutic strategy in IBD.
the nervous system plays a crucial role in maintaining intestinal homeostasis, and its modulation could be a promising strategy in IBD treatment.

we have shown that the immune response can be regulated by the enteric nervous system via a direct neuronal connection and that we have identified the molecular mechanisms underlying the neuronal control of the intestinal immune system.
